extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and self-learners in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises, propositions, and explanatory text about properties of quasicoherent and coherent sheaves: Hom, duals, support, rank, pushforwards, pullbacks, degrees of finite morphisms, and the Proj construction. Aimed at learning and verifying key technical facts used in scheme-theoretic algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(fpr, qcoh) is qcoh
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose F is a finitely presented (quasicoherent) sheaf on X, and G is a quasicoherent sheaf on X. Show that Hom(F, G) is a quasicoherent sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take a 'finite presentation' of F locally and apply the left-exact functor Hom(·, G). An explicit counterexample is given showing Hom need not be quasicoherent without finiteness hypotheses (valuation ring example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(fpr, coh) is coh
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finitely presented and G is coherent and OX is coherent, then Hom(F, G) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Exercise 14.3.A(b); relies on same local finite-presentation techniques as the qc case but with coherent hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(F,·) left-exact functor for finitely presented F
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finitely presented sheaf on X, then Hom(F, ·) gives a left-exact contravariant functor from finitely presented sheaves on X to QCoh(X) (and similarly covariant in the other argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to Exercise 2.6.H for left-exactness; the finite presentation ensures the image lands in QCoh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duals of coherent sheaves are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is coherent, its dual F^∨ := Hom(F, OX) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes duals of vector bundles. There is a canonical double-dual map F → (F^∨)^∨ which need not be an iso in general; coherent reflexive sheaves are those where it is an iso. Example: coherent sheaf from k[t]/(t) on A^1 has F^∨ = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom for finite rank locally free F is F^∨ ⊗ G
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite rank locally free sheaf and G is quasicoherent, describe an isomorphism Hom(F, G) ≅ F^∨ ⊗ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.B: prove the module-level isomorphism locally where F is free; works more generally if G is any O-module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom exactness when dualizing sequences with locally free term
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → F → G → H → 0 exact with H locally free, and E any quasicoherent sheaf, the induced sequence 0 → Hom(H,E) → Hom(G,E) → Hom(F,E) → 0 is exact (i.e., exact on the right as well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize to affine Spec A where H ≅ A^I and show the sequence splits; yields dual short exact sequence 0 → H^∨ → G^∨ → F^∨ → 0 for coherent F,G,H with H locally free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of finite type quasicoherent sheaf is closed
rubrics_metrics.description: The support of a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on a scheme X is a closed subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.D(a). In contrast, support of an arbitrary quasicoherent sheaf need not be closed — a counterexample hint is given (direct sum of skyscraper modules over C[t]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Nakayama (generators at p generate nearby)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf and sections a1,...,an generate the fiber F|_p over p, then there exists an affine open neighborhood Spec A of p such that the restrictions a1|Spec A,...,an|Spec A generate F|Spec A in various senses: generate global sections, generate each stalk, and generate each fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Exercise 14.3.E. Consequence: if F|_p = 0 then F vanishes on some neighborhood. Use Nakayama's Lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely presented + free stalk implies locally free nearby
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finitely presented and F_p is a free O_{X,p}-module for some p, then F is locally free on a neighborhood of p; hence for finitely presented sheaves local freeness is a stalk-local property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.F with hint: pick generators of the stalk, use Geometric Nakayama to get generators nearby, show kernel is finitely presented and has closed support; remove support to get a local trivialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion-free coherent sheaves on regular curves are locally free; torsion coherent sheaves supported at finitely many closed points
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Torsion-free coherent sheaves on a regular (locally Noetherian) curve are locally free. (b) Torsion coherent sheaves on a quasicompact regular integral curve are supported at a finite number of closed points. (c) Canonical short exact sequence 0 → F_tor → F → F_lf → 0 decomposing a coherent sheaf into torsion and locally free part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.G. Reduce to DVR case and use structure theorem for finitely generated modules over PID. Remarks point out hypotheses are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: finitely generated module over PID is torsion-free iff free
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a finitely generated module over a principal ideal domain, then M is torsion-free iff M is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 14.3.2; related to previous exercise and uses structure theorem for modules over PID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fiber and rank of a quasicoherent sheaf at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiber at p: F|_p := F_p / m F_p = F_p ⊗_{O_{X,p}} κ(p). Rank at p: dim_{κ(p)} F_p / m F_p (possibly infinite). On affine Spec A with M, rank is dim_{K(A/p)} M_p / p M_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with locally free rank; rank for finite type sheaves equals minimal number of local generators by Nakayama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank is additive in exact sequences (on integral scheme, at generic point)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 0 → F → G → H → 0 exact of coherent sheaves on an integral scheme, rank F − rank G + rank H = 0 (ranks taken at the generic point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.J. Warning: rank at closed points need not be additive (counterexample given on A^1_k). Use localization exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank is upper semicontinuous for finite type quasicoherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite type quasicoherent on X, then rank(F) is an upper semicontinuous function on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 14.3.K. Hint: use Geometric Nakayama that generators at a point generate nearby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant rank on a reduced scheme implies locally free
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is reduced and F is finite type quasicoherent with constant rank, then F is locally free. Moreover, finite type sheaves on a reduced scheme are locally free on a dense open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 14.3.L(a),(b). For (c) show counterexample when X is nonreduced (example with k[x]/(x^2)). Use upper semicontinuity and Nakayama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a finite morphism at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite, then π_* O_X is a finite type sheaf on Y; the rank of this sheaf at p ∈ Y is called the degree of π at p. Degree is upper semicontinuous on Y and degree at p equals the dimension of functions on the scheme-theoretic preimage π^{-1}(p) over κ(p). Degree zero iff fiber empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.3.M and surrounding discussion. Examples show degree can jump or be constant in non-obvious ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of quasicoherent sheaf under affine morphism is quasicoherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: Spec A → Spec B is a morphism of affine schemes and M is an A-module (quasicoherent sheaf on Spec A), then π_* M corresponds to M regarded as a B-module via restriction (i.e., π_* M ≅ M considered as a B-module); in particular pushforward along affine morphisms sends QCoh_X to QCoh_Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.4.A: identify sections on distinguished opens and use adjunction M ↦ M as B-module. Consequence: pushforward along affine morphism exact (Exercise 14.4.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: π_* exact for affine morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is affine, then π_* : QCoh(X) → QCoh(Y) is an exact functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.4.B follows from affine case module-level exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward under quasicompact quasiseparated morphisms sends QCoh to QCoh
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is quasicompact and quasiseparated (qcqs), then π_* of a quasicoherent sheaf F on X is quasicoherent on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.4.C (corollary to Exercise 6.2.G). Counterexamples exist without qc or qs hypotheses (reference to Stacks tag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent sheaves need not pushforward to coherent sheaves in general
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterexample: structure morphism π: A^1_k → Spec k pushes O_{A^1} (coherent) to Γ(A^1, O) = k[t], which is not a finitely generated k-module, so π_*O_{A^1} is not coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But in good situations (finite morphisms of locally Noetherian schemes, projective or proper morphisms with Noetherian hypotheses) pushforwards of coherent sheaves are coherent (Grothendieck's Coherence Theorem, Theorem 18.9.1; projective example mentioned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector bundles do not always pushforward to vector bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning: pushforward of a vector bundle need not be a vector bundle; example hint: Spec k[t]/(t) → Spec k[t].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in QCoh category instead of just locally free sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three equivalent constructions of pullback and its universal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Pullback π^* of a quasicoherent sheaf G on Y to X can be understood in three ways: (a) module-theoretic construction on affines (Γ(Spec A, π^*G) = N ⊗_B A), (b) by universal property as left-adjoint to π_*, and (c) via ringed-space inverse image and tensor: π^*G := π^{-1}G ⊗_{π^{-1}O_Y} O_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 14.5.2 discussion and 14.5.4–14.5.6. Important Exercises 14.5.A–C justify that these give the same object and that pullback exists and sends QCoh to QCoh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction: π^* left adjoint to π_* for qcqs morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is quasicompact and quasiseparated. Then (π^*: QCoh(Y) → QCoh(X), π_*: QCoh(X) → QCoh(Y)) form an adjoint pair: Hom_{OX}(π^*G, F) ≅ Hom_{OY}(G, π_*F), functorial in F and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 14.5.7; follows from universal property and earlier exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback is right-exact; flatness defined by exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y, the pullback functor π^*: QCoh(Y) → QCoh(X) is right-exact. When π^* is exact (left and right exact), we say π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.E (pullback is right-exact). Remark 14.5.8: flat morphisms give exact pullback; notion developed further in Chap.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback preserves finite type and finitely presented quasicoherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y and G is finite type (resp. finitely presented) quasicoherent on Y, then π^*G is finite type (resp. finitely presented) on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.F: cover Y by opens with surjections O_U^{⊕n} → G|_U and apply right-exact π^*. Consequence: if X locally Noetherian and G coherent then π^*G coherent; note pullback need not preserve coherence in all situations (counterexamples exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change / functoriality of pullback: (ξ◦π)^* = ξ^* π^*
rubrics_metrics.description: For morphisms ξ: W → X and π: X → Y, there is a canonical isomorphism (ξ ◦ π)^* G ≅ ξ^*(π^* G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.G. Standard functoriality of pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback on stalks and fibers
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For π: X → Y with π(p)=q, (π^* G)_p ≅ G_q ⊗_{O_{Y,q}} O_{X,p}. (b) On fibers, (π^* G)|_p ≅ G|_q ⊗_{κ(q)} κ(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.H. Possible ring-theoretic hint: (N ⊗_B A)_n ⊗_A (A/m) ≅ (N ⊗_B (A/m)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback preserves tensor products
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.I: standard compatibility of pullback with ⊗.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback need not be left-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterexample: restriction of closed subscheme exact sequence on A^1_k shows pullback is not left-exact (Exercise 14.5.J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: exact sequence 0 → O_{A^1}(-p) → O_{A^1} → O_p → 0 restrict to p to see failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Push-Pull map (base-change map) for qcqs morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative square with π and π' quasicompact and quasiseparated, there is a natural functorial map ψ^* π_* F → π'_* ψ'^* F (the push-pull or base-change map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.K: construct following general push-pull for sheaves (Def.2.7.4) and note further generalizations to cohomology later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural map from fiber of pushforward to sections on fiber (14.5.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y and q ∈ Y, there is a natural map (π_* F) ⊗ κ(q) → Γ(π^{-1}(q), F|_{π^{-1}(q)}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.5.9: this need not be iso in general; Cohomology and Base Change gives conditions when it is an iso (see Ch.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection formula
rubrics_metrics.description: For qcqs π: X → Y and F on X, G on Y, there is a natural morphism π_*(F) ⊗ G → π_*(F ⊗ π^* G). If G is locally free (or π affine) this morphism is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 14.5.L. Part (b): prove when G locally free (check for free case); part (c): when π affine the map is iso. Note terminology 'projection formula' used for several related facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety pulling back ideal sheaves; flatness preserves pullback of ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Given i: X → Y a closed embedding and base-change µ: Y' → Y, the pulled-back ideal µ^* I_{X/Y} need not equal I_{X'/Y'} in general because µ^* is only right-exact; however if µ is flat then µ^* I_{X/Y} ≅ I_{X'/Y'}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion and Exercise 14.5.J: check affine-locally the ideal of the pullback is generated by pullbacks of generators; flatness yields exactness and equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of quasicoherent sheaf from graded S-module on Proj
rubrics_metrics.description:
Given a Z_{
ge 0}-graded S-module M, one constructs a quasicoherent sheaf ~M on Proj S by taking degree-0 parts of localizations ((M_f)_0) on distinguished opens D(f) and gluing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 14.6: note reasons for degree-0 piece and gluing checks. The functor M ↦ ~M is exact (Exercise 14.6.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor from graded modules to QCoh(Proj S) is not an equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor sending graded S-modules (up to the 'agree in high degrees' relation) to quasicoherent sheaves on Proj S is not a bijection of isomorphism classes: graded modules that agree in sufficiently high degrees give the same sheaf; hence the map from graded modules (up to iso) to quasicoherent sheaves is not an equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.6.C and surrounding remarks; motivates saturation and working with finitely-generated graded modules and a modified morphism set-up to get close to equivalence for finite-type sheaves.
